√2 is Irrational

Plot fractions ever more densely and watch one hole never fill. That spot is the square root of two.

Rationals alone do not complete the number line. No fraction squares to exactly two. However fine the denominators, that spot stays empty. Numbers beyond the rationals are needed.

For example, measure a length with a 📏 ruler. However fine the marks, some lengths never match one. A square's diagonal is such a length. Fraction marks never catch it.

Examples & Exercises

Prove completely that no rational number p/qp/qp/q squares to 222 — the equation x2=2x^2 = 2x2=2 has no rational solution (Tao, Proposition 4.4.4).

(pq)2=2 has no solution pq∈Q\left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^2 = 2 \text{ has no solution } \frac{p}{q} \in \mathbb{Q}(qp​)2=2 has no solution qp​∈Q
Show proof

  1. First reduce the sign: if a rational rrr satisfies r2=2r^2 = 2r2=2, then ∣r∣|r|∣r∣ is rational, ∣r∣2=r2=2|r|^2 = r^2 = 2∣r∣2=r2=2, and r≠0r \ne 0r=0, so ∣r∣|r|∣r∣ is a positive rational solution. Hence it suffices to rule out a positive solution.

    Suppose a positive rational p/qp/qp/q with (pq)2=2\left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^2 = 2(qp​)2=2 exists. By problem 2 below, we may take p/qp/qp/q in lowest terms, i.e. gcd⁡(p,q)=1\gcd(p, q) = 1gcd(p,q)=1.

  2. Clearing denominators gives p2=2q2p^2 = 2q^2p2=2q2, so p2p^2p2 is even. If ppp were odd then p2p^2p2 would be odd (odd × odd = odd), so ppp must be even: p=2kp = 2kp=2k for a positive integer kkk.

  3. Substituting gives 4k2=2q24k^2 = 2q^24k2=2q2, i.e. q2=2k2q^2 = 2k^2q2=2k2, so q2q^2q2 is even too — and the same argument makes qqq even. But ppp and qqq both even means gcd⁡(p,q)≥2\gcd(p, q) \ge 2gcd(p,q)≥2, contradicting the lowest-terms assumption.

  4. Hence no rational squares to 222. However close a square gets to 222 — like 75\frac{7}{5}57​ or 1712\frac{17}{12}1217​ (problem 3) — no fraction lands exactly on 222: the rational line has a hole where 2\sqrt{2}2​ should be.

Prove completely, by the well-ordering principle, that every positive rational has a lowest-terms representation.

∀ r>0 rational, ∃ p,q∈N: r=pq, gcd⁡(p,q)=1\forall\, r > 0\ \text{rational},\ \exists\, p, q \in \mathbb{N}:\ r = \frac{p}{q},\ \gcd(p, q) = 1∀r>0 rational, ∃p,q∈N: r=qp​, gcd(p,q)=1
Show proof

  1. Fix a positive rational rrr. Let S={n∈N:r=m/n for some m∈N}S = \{n \in \mathbb{N} : r = m/n \text{ for some } m \in \mathbb{N}\}S={n∈N:r=m/n for some m∈N}; since r=a/br = a/br=a/b for positive integers a,ba, ba,b, we have b∈Sb \in Sb∈S — so SSS is a nonempty subset of N\mathbb{N}N.

    (Here N={1,2,3,… }\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}N={1,2,3,…}.)

  2. By the well-ordering principle, SSS has a least element q0q_0q0​. Pick p0∈Np_0 \in \mathbb{N}p0​∈N with r=p0/q0r = p_0/q_0r=p0​/q0​.

    We now show gcd⁡(p0,q0)=1\gcd(p_0, q_0) = 1gcd(p0​,q0​)=1.

  3. If d=gcd⁡(p0,q0)>1d = \gcd(p_0, q_0) > 1d=gcd(p0​,q0​)>1, then r=p0/dq0/dr = \frac{p_0/d}{q_0/d}r=q0​/dp0​/d​ with q0/d<q0q_0/d < q_0q0​/d<q0​, so q0/d∈Sq_0/d \in Sq0​/d∈S — contradicting the minimality of q0q_0q0​. Hence d=1d = 1d=1, and r=p0/q0r = p_0/q_0r=p0​/q0​ is in lowest terms.

  4. This justifies the "we may take lowest terms" step in problem 1: if some rational squared to 222, we could look at one with the smallest denominator — and it is exactly that minimal-denominator fraction that falls into the even/even contradiction.

Yet rationals squeezing 222 from both sides, like 75\frac{7}{5}57​ and 1712\frac{17}{12}1217​, are easy to find (in the model the shortest distance shrinks 0.0142→0.00245→⋯0.0142 \to 0.00245 \to \cdots0.0142→0.00245→⋯ as NNN grows), and together with the general estimate above this shows the rationals get as close as one likes to the 2\sqrt{2}2​ slot, but never touch it.

    The number filling this hole is the 2\sqrt{2}2​ whose existence the least-upper-bound axiom guarantees (the n-th root scene).
